edition.window: Orders and decisions passed or reported between 11:00 AM IST on 16 October 2026 and 11:00 AM IST on 19 October 2026

items.caseName: Dr. Ravi Gupta v. Commercial Law Publishers (India) Pvt. Ltd.
items.coram: Ashok Kumar Bhardwaj (Judicial Member) and Atul Chaturvedi (Technical Member)
items.headline: Author's royalty can be operational debt, but claim falls short
items.text: The NCLT accepted that royalty payable under a publishing agreement can be an operational debt, following the NCLAT's Jaipur Trade Expocentre ruling. It still dismissed the author's insolvency petition against the law publisher because the invoices and admitted amount did not support the claimed default of about Rs 1.17 crore, and an extra shortfall for 2023-24 had no invoice behind it.

items.caseName: Punjab National Bank v. SVOGL Oil Gas and Energy Limited
items.coram: Justice Anupinder Singh Grewal (President) and Ravindra Chaturvedi (Technical Member)
items.headline: Pending winding-up no bar to CIRP; SVOGL admitted
items.text: The NCLT admitted PNB's petition against SVOGL, holding that a winding-up ordered by the Delhi High Court in 2017 and later transferred to the NCLT does not block insolvency where no irreversible steps have been taken. PNB's claim was put at about Rs 1,526.95 crore. A moratorium was declared, an interim resolution professional appointed and the Official Liquidator told to hand over the company's assets and records.

items.caseName: Venkatavarathan Narasimhan Iyengar v. Committee of Creditors of Somerset Constructions Private Limited
items.coram: K. R. Saji Kumar (Judicial Member) and Anil Raj Chellan (Technical Member)
items.headline: Fresh CIRP round not a matter of course
items.text: The NCLT refused to treat late expressions of interest from two companies as resolution plans, since neither had joined the original process. It regularised the CIRP period and gave the resolution professional 120 days for a fresh process with a new Form G, open to all eligible applicants on equal terms, and dismissed the suspended director's intervention plea.

items.caseName: Bajaj Healthcare Limited v. Mr. Rajesh Kumar Mittal
items.coram: K. R. Saji Kumar (Judicial Member) and Anil Raj Chellan (Technical Member)
items.headline: Bajaj Healthcare gets GENRX as going concern, clean slate
items.text: The NCLT partly allowed Bajaj Healthcare's application after it bought GENRX Pharmaceuticals as a going concern in a liquidation e-auction for about Rs 10.89 crore. The buyer was shielded from liabilities up to the liquidation commencement date and a share capital restructuring was approved, but requests for automatic continuation of licences and blanket tax benefits were declined.

items.caseName: Balakrishnan Baburajan v. Murali Narayanan and Ors.
items.coram: Vinay Goel (Judicial Member) and Ravichandran Ramasamy (Technical Member)
items.headline: All directors answerable to liquidator for company cash
items.text: The NCLT rejected the directors' plea that only the former managing director ran the company, holding their responsibility for its assets joint and several. Six directors of Goodwin Packpet were told to deposit the cash balance shown in the accounts into the liquidation account within 30 days with interest. A receivable from the former MD's proprietorship was left to a separate recovery action, as it cannot be recovered summarily under Sections 19(2) and 34(3) IBC.

items.caseName: The Regional Provident Fund Commissioner-II v. Mr. R Raghavendran
items.coram: Vinay Goel (Judicial Member) and Ravichandran Ramasamy (Technical Member)
items.headline: EPFO claim without prior assessment not admissible in liquidation
items.text: The NCLT upheld the liquidator's rejection of EPFO's Rs 59.46 lakh claim against Peejay Agro Foods, since no assessment or damages order under Sections 7A, 7Q or 14B of the EPF Act existed before the CIRP began. Following the NCLAT's Rachna Jhunjhunwala ruling, it held notional interest and damages are not crystallised dues, and found no proof that the earlier partnership firm became the company.

items.caseName: Mehul Vyas v. Fiba Shipping Agency & Ors.
items.coram: Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma (Judicial Member), Arun Baroka and Indevar Pandey (Technical Members)
items.headline: No solo appeal after skipping the group remedy; Rs 5 lakh costs
items.text: The NCLAT held that a shop-owning shareholder of Dreams the Mall, Bhandup could not separately attack the NCLT Mumbai's restructuring order after not using the representative remedy available to shop owners as a group. It relied on a structural audit showing the mall was repairable, dismissed the appeal as not maintainable and imposed Rs 5 lakh exemplary costs.

items.caseName: Yash Raj Films Private Limited v. Commissioner of CGST & Central Excise, Mumbai West
items.coram: S.K. Mohanty (Judicial Member) and M.M. Parthiban (Technical Member)
items.headline: No service tax on overseas film-shoot arrangers
items.text: The CESTAT treated foreign local area representatives who arranged services for overseas shoots as intermediaries, so the place of provision was outside India under Rule 9(c) of the Place of Provision of Services Rules, 2012 and reverse charge did not apply. It set aside a demand of about Rs 46.41 crore with interest and penalties, deciding on merits without reaching limitation.

items.caseName: Reliable Enterprises v. Commissioner of CGST & Central Excise, Patna
items.coram: Ashok Jindal (Judicial Member) and K. Anpazhakan (Technical Member)
items.headline: SIM distributor commission exempt from service tax
items.text: The CESTAT held commission earned from Vodafone exempt under Serial No. 29(f) of Notification 25/2012-ST, and treated supply of dustbins and portable toilets to local bodies as VAT-paid sales of goods. Demands up to September 2016 were time-barred, but tax with interest, without penalty, was upheld on certain works contract services for October 2016 to June 2017.
